body: Indian disclosure rules give retail unusually good visibility into institutional behaviour: monthly MF portfolios, quarterly shareholding patterns, and daily bulk/block deals. Indian PMS houses like Marcellus layer forensic accounting filters in front of quality/moat analysis. Meanwhile, most active Indian funds still trail their benchmarks over 5–10 years.
title: institutional_process › Takeaway

body:
1. **Segment, not consolidated, data.** Find the small, fast-growing segment hidden inside a big, flat company. Examples: NVIDIA data center in FY16–18, Radico Prestige & Above, Royal Enfield inside Eicher's truck-heavy group.
2. **Mix shift → margin → operating leverage.** Revenue +44% turned into PAT +239% at Radico (FY17–21). Watch gross margin and A&P spend in concall commentary.
3. **Balance-sheet inflection.** Deleveraging (Radico D/E 0.77 → 0.15) both raises equity value and triggers the rerating.
4. **Policy documents as order-book precursors.** Defence indigenisation, PLI and China+1 come first. Map first-order beneficiaries (OEMs: HAL, BEL, Dixon), then second-order (component/subsystem suppliers), then third-order (raw materials, testing, logistics).
5. **Competitor distress / industry structure change.** When a leader is distracted (USL under Mallya's debt and then the Diageo transition; wind OEM consolidation after Suzlon's collapse), challengers can gain share. Verify with channel checks (retail shelves, dealer waiting periods such as Royal Enfield's months-long waiting lists **[UNVERIFIED]**).
6. **Read the concall for capacity utilisation and capex language.** A company at more than 80% utilisation announcing a brownfield expansion is the precursor to an earnings step-up (Deepak's phenol plant, Dixon's mobile lines).
7. **Insider/promoter behaviour.** Promoter buying and no pledging. Radico's promoter refusing to sell a stake to Mallya is the anecdotal form.
8. **Valuation starting point.** The largest returns (Radico, defence) had both engines: earnings 5–8x and P/E 2–5x. NVIDIA after 2023 shows that earnings alone can carry the move, but buying at already-high multiples removes one engine and adds derating risk.

title: multibagger_case_studies › Inferences (a synthesised checklist drawn from the cases)

body: Multibaggers are rare and violent. In the US, **4% of stocks explain all net wealth creation since 1926** and the majority underperform T-bills. Globally, about **2.4%** of firms create all net wealth. Almost every big winner had a 50–95% drawdown along the way. The same patterns (policy tailwind, sector boom, turnaround) produced spectacular failures, such as Suzlon's 99.6% wipeout.

body:

| OPM | 9% | 12% | 11% | 10% | 10% | 15% | 14% | 14% |
| PAT | 21 | 31 | 34 | 30 | 21 | 53 | 64 | 65 |

**Shareholding**

| | Jun25 | Sep25 | Dec25 | Mar26 | Jun26 | Sep26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Promoter | 52.62 | 52.62 | 52.62 | 57.48 | 62.28 | 62.28 |
| FII | 2.59 | 2.25 | 2.08 | 1.72 | 4.87 | 7.26 |
| DII | 0.02 | 0.05 | 0.03 | 0.02 | 0.43 | 0.30 |

- The promoter stake rose about 9.7 percentage points through open-market buying (NCVI Enterprises and Mayadevi Polycot, March 2026) with no new shares issued. Equity capital stayed at ₹59 cr.
- The promoter disclosed no encumbrance for FY26.
- FII holding has tripled in two quarters.

**Structural story and named cause**
- Product mix is shifting away from ibuprofen. Non-ibuprofen APIs reached 45% of pharma revenue in Q2 FY27 (38% a year earlier), with that line growing about 70% YoY.
- Pharma segment EBIT nearly doubled (35.5 to 68.1). Chemicals EBIT also improved.
- Q2 FY27 numbers: revenue ₹795 cr (+40%), EBITDA ₹115 cr (+80%), PAT ₹65 cr (2.2x). Guided EBITDA margin is 14-15% (FPJ, Multibagg, Sahi).
- This is a Radico-style mix shift combined with heavy promoter buying, the strongest insider signal in the set.
- Debtor days have crept up (79 to 95), CFO/EBITDA was 93% in FY26 and capex is self-funded (CWIP of ₹189 cr).

**Bull case**
- If FY28 sales reach ₹3,600 cr at 15% OPM, PAT would be about ₹330 cr. At 22-25x, market cap would be ₹7.3-8.3k cr, 1.3-1.5x.
- Real multibagger upside needs ROCE to move toward 18-20%. FY20-21 (30% OPM) shows what operating leverage can do.

**Risks**
- P/E of 27.7x on TTM is already at the top of the allowed range.
- ROCE of 11% is low.
- The stock has already rerated, from a 52-week low of ~₹67 to a high of ~₹224 and ₹192 now.
- Ibuprofen pricing is cyclical and exposed to Chinese supply.
- The promoter stake is now 62%, so further buying is limited by takeover rules.

**Kill criteria**
- OPM below 12% for two quarters.
- Non-ibuprofen share stalls below 40%.
- The promoter sells.
- Debtor days above 110.
- **Entry discipline:** wait for Q3 FY27 confirmation or a P/E ≤22x on TTM.

data.section: Finalist 2: IOL Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals (IOLCP). Conviction 64/100. WATCHLIST (near buy-zone)

title: quant_pattern_hunt › Finalist 2: IOL Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals (IOLCP). Conviction 64/100. WATCHLIST (near buy-zone)

body:
- **Misses get explained, and often unprompted.** The Q4FY26 and Q1/Q2FY27 opening remarks open with what went wrong: Middle East war (~INR 380-400 cr of Q4 revenue deferred), LPG and election-driven labour shortages, JJM water payments, metro hand-over delays, INR 450-600 cr of collections slipping past quarter-end. That is why the candour index (31%) is well above Skipper's 12.5%.
- **But targets are re-set silently.** Nine moved goalposts: NWC 100 -> 110 -> 110 again for the next year; civil 25% -> 10-15%; FY27 margin -> FY28 -> FY29; cables FY27 3,400-3,500 -> 2,500-2,600; net debt 5,500 -> 6,000. The explanation of the miss is volunteered; the fact that a specific number was promised is not.
- **Guidance mostly comes from Q&A.** 64 of 75 promises were extracted by analyst questions; the opening remarks rarely state FY guidance. Prompted numbers delivered 22%, volunteered ones 48%.
- **Credibility fell as conditions worsened:** promises made in FY25 calls delivered 53%, in FY26 calls 20%. Same shape as Skipper (56% -> 25%), at a lower level.
- **A recurring "one more quarter" pattern on cash:** every quarter from Q2FY26 to Q2FY27 attributes high debt to collections that "came in the first week" of the next month (Saudi in Jan-26, INR 450 cr in Apr-26, INR 600 cr in Oct-26). Each was true, but the quarter-end debt kept rising.

**How to use this.** Treat KEC's group margin, debt and NWC guidance as a direction, not a number: on this record, haircut margin-expansion promises by ~90% and expect quarter-end debt above guidance. Segment growth and plant dates need a 2-3 quarter haircut. Under-promising has been consistent only in SAE and cables.
